He played [[college basketball]] for [[Hutchinson Community College]] and [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]]. ==High school== In high school he first played for [[Laney High School]], and in his senior year he played guard for [[New Hanover High School]] in his hometown of [[Wilmington, North Carolina]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.collegeinsider.com/contributor/column128/kadeem-allens-improbable-journey|title=Collegeinsider | Kadeem Allen's Improbable Journey|website=www.collegeinsider.com}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.wwaytv3.com/new-hanover-grad-kadeem-allen-signs-two-way-deal-with-the-new-york-knicks/|title=New Hanover grad Kadeem Allen signs two-way deal wit New York Knicks|date=January 16, 2019}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/132535/kadeem-allen|title=Kadeem Allen – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles – ESPN|website=ESPN.com}}{{Cite web|url=https://portcitydaily.com/community-and-events/2016/11/10/sports-ncaa-basketball-arizona-kadeem-allen-170416/|title=College basketball: Wilmington standout Kadeem Allen looking for big year at University of Arizona (video)|first=Joe|last=Catenacci|date=November 10, 2016}} ==College career== Playing for [[Hutchinson Community College]] in [[Hutchinson, Kansas]], Allen as a freshman averaged 17.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.5 steals (tops in the [[Kansas Jayhawk Community College Conference|Jayhawk Conference]]), and 3.9 assists (3rd) in 2012–13. As a sophomore he scored 25.9 points per game (second in the [[NJCAA]]), and had 5.9 assists and 2.3 steals per game. He was named Junior College Player of the Year in 2014 by both the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] and [[NJCAA]] after being named the 2014 NJCAA Preseason Player of the Year by the ''[[Sporting News]]''.{{Cite web|url=https://arizonawildcats.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/kadeem-allen/5303|title=Kadeem Allen – Men's Basketball|website=University of Arizona Athletics}} Hutchinson transferred to the [[University of Arizona]] and played for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] for his final two years. He averaged 9.8 points, 1.6 steals (4th in the Pac-12), and 4.0 rebounds per game in his senior campaign.{{cite news|title=New Hanover grad invited to Hornets' workout|url=http://www.walb.com/story/35604180/new-hanover-grad-invited-to-hornets-workout|access-date=June 22, 2017|work=WALB|date=June 6, 2017|archive-date=December 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171213010158/http://www.walb.com/story/35604180/new-hanover-grad-invited-to-hornets-workout|url-status=dead}} As a senior, he was named second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and to the All-Defensive team.{{Cite web|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2017/3/6/2016-17-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors.aspx|title=2016–17 Pac-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference Honors|website=Pac-12 Conference|access-date=June 23, 2017}} ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics (2017–2018)=== Allen was drafted by the Celtics in the [[2017 NBA draft]]{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Forsberg|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19711028/2017-nba-draft-boston-celtics-take-jayson-tatum-no-3-overall-pick|title=Duke's Jayson Tatum selected No. 3 overall by Celtics|work=ESPN.com|date=June 22, 2017|access-date=April 28, 2018}} and signed the franchise's first [[two-way contract]]. Under the terms of the deal, he will split time between the Celtics and their G League affiliate, the [[Maine Red Claws]].{{cite news|title=Boston Celtics Sign Kadeem Allen |url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-sign-kadeem-allen|access-date=July 20, 2017|work=[[Boston Celtics]]|date=July 19, 2017}} On January 29, 2018, Allen was named the [[NBA G League]] Player of the Week following a 38 points per game over the prior week. It included a 46 point game against the [[Long Island Nets]] on January 23.{{cite news|url=http://gleague.nba.com/news/kadeem-allen-named-nba-g-league-player-week/|title=Kadeem Allen Named NBA G League Player of the Week|date=January 29, 2018|work=[[National Basketball Association]]|access-date=January 30, 2018}} On February 2, 2018, Allen and teammate [[Jabari Bird]] were named to the Midseason All-NBA G League East Team after averaging 18.0 points, 5.9 rebounds, 5.0 assists, and 2.6 steals per game.{{cite news|url=http://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/allen-bird-midseason/|title=Allen, Bird Named to Midseason All-NBA G League Team|date=February 2, 2018|work=[[National Basketball Association]]|access-date=February 3, 2018|archive-date=February 2, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180202231312/http://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/allen-bird-midseason/|url-status=dead}} On July 15, 2018, Allen was waived by the Celtics.{{cite web |title=We have waived guard Kadeem Allen. |url=https://twitter.com/celtics/status/1018597352112836608 |website=Boston Celtics on Twitter |access-date=July 15, 2018 |date=July 15, 2018}} ===Westchester 2021.{{cite web|title=Charge Acquire Kristian Doolittle|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-acquire-kristian-doolittle|date=February 6, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=February 6, 2021}}
